questions.q: Consider three boxes, each containing $10$ balls labelled $1, 2, \ldots . , 10$. Suppose one ball is randomly drawn from each of the boxes. Denote by ${n}_{i}$, the label of the ball drawn from the $i^{th}$ box,  \left(i = 1, 2, 3\right)$. Then, the number of ways in which the balls can be chosen such that ${n}_{1} < {n}_{2} < {n}_{3}$ is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Each box contains $10$ balls numbered from $1$ to $10$.

${n}_{1}, {n}_{2}, {n}_{3}$ are numbers on the balls drawn from the box ${B}_{1}, {B}_{2}$ and ${B}_{3}$ respectively such that ${n}_{1} < {n}_{2} < {n}_{3}$.

i.e., all $3$ numbers ${n}_{1}, {n}_{2}, {n}_{3}$ must be different and can be arranged only in one way (increasing).

Now ${n}_{1}, {n}_{2}, {n}_{3}$ can be selected in $10{C}_{3}$ ways.

Hence, total number of ways ${=}^{10}{C}_{3} . 1{=}^{10}{C}_{3} = \left(10 !\right)\left(3 !\right)\left(7 !\right) = \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8}{3 \times 2} = 120$.

questions.q: The number of triplets  \left(x, y, z\right)$~where $x, y, z$~are distinct non negative integers satisfying $x + y + z = 15$, is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$x + y + z = 15$

Now we know that,

Non-negative integral solution of equation~$a + b + c = n$~is given by~$C3 - 1 n + 3 - 1$~where~$a = b = c \text{ and } a = b \ne c$~are also possibilities

So by above formula we get,

Total number of non-negative solution will be, $C3 - 1 15 + 3 - 1 = C2 17$

Now solving~If any of these $2$ are equal
So, the equation will become$x + 2y = 15$

Now finding possible cases we get,

$\begin{cases}y = 0 & x = 15\end{cases}$

$\begin{cases}y = 1 & x = 13\end{cases}$

$\begin{cases}y = 2 & x = 11\end{cases}$

$\begin{cases}y = 3 & x = 9\end{cases}$

$\begin{cases}y = 4 & x = 7\end{cases}$

$y = 5x = 5 \to x = y = z = 5$

$y = 6x = 3$

$y = 7x = 1$

So, total possibilities where~$x, y \text{ and } z$~are distinct will be,

$= C2 17 - C2 3 \times 8 + 2$

{Note adding~$2$~because the cases~$x = y = z$~is subtracted three times}

$= 136 - 24 + 2 = 114$

questions.q: All the letters of the word PUBLIC are written in all possible orders and these words are written as in a dictionary with serial numbers. Then the serial number of the word PUBLIC is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:${P}_{1}, {P}_{2} \ldots , {P}_{15}$~be~$15$~points on circle.

$∴$Total number of triangles$= C3 15$

When~$i + j + k = 15$~then possible cases are

$i = 1, j + k = 14 ⇒ ( 2, 12 ) , ( 3, 11 ) , ( 4, 10 ) , ( 5, 9 ) , ( 6, 8 ) = 5$~ways

$i = 2, j + k = 13 ⇒ ( 3, 10 ) , \ldots \ldots \ldots . , ( 6, 7 ) = 4$~ways

$i = 3, j + k = 12 ⇒ ( 4, 8 ) , ( 5, 7 ) = 2$~ways

$i = 4, j + k = 11 ⇒ ( 5, 6 ) = 1$~way

Hence, there are total~$12$~ways for~$i + j + k = 15$.

$∴$ The number of possible triangles using the vertices ${P}_{i}, {P}_{j}, {P}_{k}$ such that $i + j + k \ne 15$~is equal to $C3 15 - 12 = 455 - 12 = 443$.

questions.q: The number of $9$~digit numbers, that can be formed using all the digits of the number $123412341$ so that the even digits occupy only even places, is ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
According to the question,

$1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4$

there are four even~digits as~$2$ and $4$ are repeating two times each.~
So,~the even digits will occupy the even places in~$\dfrac{4 !}{( 2 ! 2 ! )} = 6$ ways

$3$ and $1$ are repeating two and three times~respectively.
So, the remaining places will be occupied by odd~digits in $\dfrac{5 !}{( 3 ! 2 ! )} = 10$ ways

Therefore, total $9$~digits that can be formed $= 6 \times 10 = 60$.
Hence, the answer is~$60$.

questions.q: In an examination of Mathematics paper, there are $20$ questions of equal marks and the question paper is divided into three sections : $A, B$ and $C$. A student is required to attempt total $15$ questions taking at least $4$ questions from each section. If section $A$ has $8$ questions, section $B$ has $6$ questions and section $C$ has $6$ questions, then the total number of ways a student can select $15$ questions is _________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Mathematics paper has $20$ questions of equal marks

and have three sections $A, B & C$, also $A$ has $8$ questions, $B$ has $6$ questions and $C$ has $6$ questions,

Now, if $4$ questions from each section are selected,

then remaining $3$ questions can be selected either in $( 1, 1, 1 )$ or $( 3, 0, 0 )$ or $( 2, 1, 0 )$ {as we have already selected $4 \times 3 = 12$ questions}

So, the total ways will be$= C5 8 \cdot C5 6 \cdot C5 6 + C6 8 C5 6 \cdot C4 6 \times 2 +C5 8 \cdot C6 6 \cdot C4 6 \times 2 + C4 8 \cdot C6 6 \cdot C5 6 \times 2 + C7 8 \cdot C4 6 \cdot C4 6$

$= 56 \cdot 6 \cdot 6 + 28 \cdot 6 \cdot 15 \cdot 2 + 56 \cdot 15 \cdot 2 + 70 \cdot 6 \cdot 2 + 8 \cdot 15 \cdot 15$

$= 2016 + 5040 + 1680 + 840 + 1800 = 11376$

questions.q: There are $5$ students in class $10, 6$ students in class $11$ and $8$ students in class $12 .$~If the number of ways, in which $10$ students can be selected from them so as to include at least $2$ students from each class and at most $5$ students from the total $11$ students of class $10$ and $11$ is $100k,$~then $k$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{cases}Class & {10}^{th} & {11}^{th} & {12}^{th} \\ Totalstudent & 5 & 6 & 8\end{cases}$

From these students, we can choose two students from class~$10$, three students from class~$11 \text{ and } 5$~students from class~$12 .$

So, total number of ways is~$C2 5 \times C3 6 \times C5 8$

Again, From these students, we can choose two students from class~$10,$~two students from class~$11 \text{ and } 6$~students from class~$12 .$

Number of selection~$= C2 5 \times C2 6 \times C6 8$

Again, from these students, we can choose three students from class~$10$, two students from class~$11 \text{ and } 5$~students from class~$12 .$~So, total number of ways is $C3 5 \times C2 6 \times C5 8$

$⇒$ Total number of ways $= \left(C2 5 \times C3 6 \times C5 8\right) + \left(C2 5 \timesC2 6 \timesC6 8\right) + \left(C3 5 \timesC2 6 \timesC5 8\right)$~$= \left(C2 5 \timesC3 6 \timesC3 8\right) + \left(C2 5 \timesC2 6 \timesC2 8\right) + \left(C2 5 \timesC2 6 \timesC3 8\right)$

$= \left(\dfrac{5 \times 4}{2 \times 1} \times \dfrac{6 \times 5 \times 4}{3 \times 2 \times 1} \times \dfrac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{3 \times 2 \times 1}\right) + \left(\dfrac{5 \times 4}{2 \times 1} \times \dfrac{6 \times 5}{2 \times 1} \times \dfrac{8 \times 7}{2 \times 1}\right) + \left(\dfrac{5 \times 4}{2 \times 1} \times \dfrac{6 \times 5}{2 \times 1} \times \dfrac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{3 \times 2 \times 1}\right)$

$= 23800$

According to question $100k = 23800$

$⇒ k = 238$

questions.q: The total number of $3 -$digit numbers whose sum of digits is~$10$, is ..........
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $xyz$~be the three-digit number such that

$x + y + z = 10, x \ge 1, y \ge 0, z \ge 0$

Let~$x - 1 = t ⇒ x = 1 + t$

So,~$x \ge 1 ⇒ t + 1 \ge 1 ⇒ t \ge 0$

Also,~$x + y + z = 10 ⇒ t + y + z = 10 - 1 = 9$

So,~$t + y + z = 9, 0 \le t, y, z \le 9$

Thus, total number of non-negative integral solution~$= C3 - 1 9 + 3 - 1 = C2 11 = \dfrac{11 . 10}{2} = 55$

But for~$t = 9, x = 10$, so required number of integers~$= 55 - 1 = 54$.
